card.title: Ideal gas and ideal gas equation; universal gas constant and its significance

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Three empirical laws fold into one equation. Boyle contributes V ∝ 1/P, Charles contributes V ∝ T, Avogadro contributes V ∝ n; multiplied together they give V ∝ nT/P, and the constant that makes it an equality is **R — the universal gas constant**, 0.0821 L·atm/mol·K in laboratory units, 8.314 J/mol·K in SI, 1.987 cal/mol·K in thermochemistry, and identical for every gas — the experimental soul of Avogadro's law.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - PV = nRT - R = 0.0821 L·atm/mol·K = 8.314 J/mol·K = 1.987 cal/mol·K - n = PV/RT; m = nM - d = PM/RT; M = dRT/P - k = R/N_A = 1.38 × 10⁻²³ J/K

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Density form vs moles form:** d = PM/RT needs M in g/mol and d in g/L; using n where M belongs doubles the error.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: "The ideal gas equation PV = nRT combines Boyle's law, Charles's law and Avogadro's law; the constant R has the same value for all gases."

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***The tyre pressure gauge*** — a tyre reading 32 psi at 20 °C climbs near 35 psi after highway driving: PV = nRT with V, n fixed makes P ∝ T — Charles's law wearing rubber.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Verified PYQs: NEB 2023 and NEB 2024 — state Boyle's and Charles's laws and derive the ideal gas equation (solved above). Other items are NEB-style practice.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — One Equation to Rule the Gas Laws PV = nRT compresses Boyle, Charles and Avogadro into four symbols, and its constant R is the most travelled number in physical chemistry — the same 8.314 J/mol·K (or 0.0821 L·atm/mol·K) that later powers entropy, equilibrium and electrochemistry.…  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 The derivation (Boyle + Charles + Avogadro) - Let n moles of gas occupy volume V at pressure P and temperature T. - **Boyle:** V ∝ 1/P (T, n fixed). **Charles:** V ∝ T (P, n fixed). **Avogadro:** V ∝ n (T, P fixed). - Combining all three: **V ∝ nT/P** → V = R·nT/P → **PV = nRT**.…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Derivation chain: "Boyle + Charles + Avogadro → PV = nRT". R table: 0.0821 (L·atm), 8.314 (J), 2 (cal). Density trick: d = PM/RT. Kelvin check before plugging.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **NEB 2023/2024 (4m): State Boyle's law and Charles's law. Derive the ideal gas equation from them.** — **Boyle's law:** at constant temperature, the volume of a given mass of gas is inversely proportional to its pressure — V ∝ 1/P, or P₁V₁ = P₂V₂.…  ·  **NEB-style (2m): Calculate the pressure exerted by 0.5 mol of an ideal gas occupying a 5 L vessel at 300 K (R = 0.0821 L atm/mol K).** — From PV = nRT: P = nRT/V = (0.5 mol × 0.0821 L·atm/mol·K × 300 K)/5 L = 12.315/5 = **2.46 atm**. (Unit check: mol cancels mol, K cancels K, litres divide litres — leaving atm.)

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: In the derivation, state each contributing law with its constant variables, then combine in one line — examiners look for the three proportionalities explicitly before PV = nRT appears.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: R's universality is the experimental fact behind Avogadro's law: one constant for all gases means equal n gives equal V at the same P and T.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Derivation: Boyle (V ∝ 1/P) + Charles (V ∝ T) + Avogadro (V ∝ n) → V ∝ nT/P → PV = nRT. R = 0.0821 L·atm/mol·K = 8.314 J/mol·K = 1.987 cal/mol·K; universal for all ideal gases. Check: 1 atm × 22.4 L / (1 mol × 273 K) = 0.0821. Boltzmann k = R/N_A = 1.38 × 10⁻²³ J/K. Forms: n = PV/RT; d = PM/RT; M = dRT/P.…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Planetary atmospheres are ideal-gas territory: the same PV = nRT with Mars's 6 mbar CO₂ and Earth's 1 bar N₂ explains why density, not composition, sets scale heights.

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: **NEB-style (2m): The density of a gas is 1.96 g/L at 1 atm and 273 K. Calculate its molar mass and identify the gas.** — From the density form of the ideal gas equation, d = PM/RT, so M = dRT/P. Substituting: M = (1.96 g/L × 0.0821 L·atm/mol·K × 273 K)/1 atm = **44 g/mol**.…

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 3. Scientific Definitions | Term | Scientific meaning | Value | |---|---|---| | **Ideal gas** | Obeys PV = nRT at all T and P | Hypothetical | | **Universal gas constant** | Proportionality constant of the ideal equation | 0.0821 L·atm/mol·K | | **R in SI** | Energy per mole per kelvin | 8.314 J/mol·K | | **Boltzmann constant** | R per molecule | 1.38 × 10⁻²³ J/K | |…  ·  ## 4. Detailed Explanation ### 4.1 Verified PYQ (NEB 2023 + 2024): state Boyle's and Charles's laws; derive the ideal gas equation - **Boyle's law:** at constant temperature, the volume of a fixed mass of gas is inversely proportional to its pressure (P₁V₁ = P₂V₂).…  ·  ### Deep dive — R is the bridge between the mechanical and the thermal PV = nRT compresses all the gas laws into one line, and the universal gas constant R = 8.314 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹ = 0.0821 L atm K⁻¹ mol⁻¹ is its pivot.…

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Derive PV = nRT from Boyle's and Charles's laws and state the value of R in two unit systems.  ·  A 10 L flask holds 2 mol gas at 27 °C; find the pressure in atm.  ·  A gas has density 3.17 g/L at STP; identify it from its molar mass.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: **Values and uses of R** | Form of R | Value | Use with units | Example | |---|---|---|---| | SI | 8.314 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹ | P in Pa, V in m³ | P = nRT/V for 0.5 mol in 0.01 m³ at 300 K → 1.25 × 10⁵ Pa | | Litre-atmosphere | 0.0821 L atm K⁻¹ mol⁻¹ | P in atm, V in L | V of 2 mol at 1 atm, 273 K = 44.6 L | | Calorie form |…  ·  ## 5. Comparison Tables **R in its three costumes** | Form | Value | Use when | |---|---|---| | L·atm/mol·K | 0.0821 | P in atm, V in litres | | J/mol·K | 8.314 | SI: Pa and m³; energy contexts | | cal/mol·K | 1.987 | Thermochemistry | **From partial laws to full equation** | Law | Contribution | Recovered by holding…  ·  ## 6. Common Confusions **R is not "8.314 always":** the value must match the pressure–volume units; 0.0821 with atm–litres, 8.314 with Pa–m³.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: **Temperature in Kelvin again:** PV = nRT inherits Charles's absolute scale; a Celsius slip scales the answer by 273/300 or worse.  ·  **Ideal gases do not exist:** the equation is a limiting model; real gases approach it at low pressure and high temperature but never coincide.  ·  ## 7. Exam Application **Verified PYQ (NEB 2023/2024): State Boyle's law and Charles's law. Derive the ideal gas equation.** — Boyle: V ∝ 1/P at constant T and n. Charles: V ∝ T at constant P and n. Combining: V ∝ T/P for fixed n; adding Avogadro's V ∝ n: V ∝ nT/P.…
